Was checking without an object normally makes the subject the person doing the checking.'),
 C('Show earlier completion.','The figures had been checked before the meeting.\nThe repair will have been completed by Friday.\n\nPerfect passive: have + been + participle, with had or will have where the timeline requires it.','Keep the required earlier-past or future-deadline meaning. Do not add been only because an action is finished.'),
 C('Use passive forms after modals and other verbs.','The parcel must be signed for.\nThe email should have been sent earlier.\nThe form needs to be completed.\nI dislike being interrupted.','After a modal use be; after a modal-perfect have use been. Preserve a required preposition such as for in signed for.'),
 C('Choose by, with or no extra phrase.','The mural was painted by local artists. → doers\nThe box was opened with a key. → tool\nMy bag has been found. → the finder need not be named\n\nAn agent phrase is optional when it adds nothing useful.','Some adjectives and passives overlap: The door is closed can describe a state. A by-phrase is a useful clue, not a perfect test in every sentence.'),
 C('Recognise special patterns and limits.','They gave her a ticket. → She was given a ticket.\nThey made us wait. → We were made to wait.\nHe got promoted. → informal passive\n\nAn accident happened. has no ordinary passive because happen has no object.','Let has no normal matching passive in this use; say We were allowed to leave. Do not mechanically attach be and a participle to every verb.'),
 C('Explain a process clearly.','A suitcase is tagged, moved and sometimes delayed. Passive voice can keep the bag as the topic while describing different stages.\n\nRevisit Olivia’s recording for how the tracking process connects the bag to its owner.','The new questions follow the process and its conditions. The recording describes typical cases, not a promise that every bag is returned on a fixed date.')
];

 G('choice','Which passive keeps the present-simple routine?','The bags are scanned every morning.','Are scanned is present simple passive, preserving the routine indicated by every morning.','Identify both voice and time.  G('gap','The bag has ___ found. Complete the present-perfect passive.','been','Has been found combines present perfect with passive voice, making the bag the receiver of the finding.','Found is already the participle. Complete the passive auxiliary group after has.'),
 G('order','Build a past passive without an unnecessary agent.','The suitcase was returned yesterday.','Was returned keeps the suitcase as subject and describes a completed past event.','Keep the receiver first, then the past form of be and the participle. The time word belongs at the end.'),
 G('edit','Correct the continuous passive: The road is repaired right now by the workers. Use an in-progress form.','The road is being repaired right now by the workers.','Is being repaired explicitly describes the repair in progress, unlike the present-simple passive.','The prompt asks for activity in progress at this moment. Add the continuous passive element before the participle.'),
 G('choice','Which phrase identifies the doer?','by the airport staff','By introduces the agent of a passive action, while with commonly introduces a tool or material.','Look for the people performing the action, rather than the instrument used to carry it out.',['by the airport staff','with a scanner','at the claim desk']),
 G('gap','The parcel must ___ signed for. Complete the modal passive.','be','A modal is followed by be plus the past participle in this passive pattern, retaining the preposition for.','Must is already the modal. Use the base passive auxiliary before signed, without changing the final preposition.'),
 G('choice','Which sentence has a continuous passive?','The bag was being checked.','Was being checked places the bag as receiver of an activity in progress in the past.','Look for both being and a participle. A continuous active form would identify the checker as its subject.',['The bag was being checked.','The staff were checking the bag.','The bag had been checked.']),
 G('order','Build a passive result completed before a future deadline.','The bridge will have been completed by July.','Will have been completed is future perfect passive, with by July identifying the deadline.','Keep the future-perfect auxiliary sequence together. The completion participle follows been.'),
 G('edit','Remove the impossible passive: An accident was happened yesterday.','An accident happened yesterday.','Happen is intransitive in this use, so there is no object that can become the subject of a passive.','The subject is the event itself.  G('gap','The email should have ___ sent earlier. Complete the modal-perfect passive.','been','Should have been sent evaluates a past action and makes the email the receiver of sending.','Have is already present after the modal. Complete the perfect passive auxiliary group before the participle.'),
 G('choice','Which change preserves the past time?','They repaired it yesterday. → It was repaired yesterday.','The past-simple active becomes past-simple passive, retaining yesterday and the completed repair.','Keep the time reference while changing the focus. A new present-perfect form would not preserve this dated-past pattern.',['They repaired it yesterday. → It was repaired yesterday.','They repaired it yesterday. → It is repaired tomorrow.','They repaired it yesterday. → It has repairing yesterday.']),
 G('rewrite','Make the bag the subject: Someone has found the bag.','The bag has been found.','The present-perfect passive keeps the time and result while omitting the unknown or unimportant finder.','Move the original object to subject position. Retain has and add the perfect-passive auxiliary before found.'),
 G('order','Build a passive with an instrument phrase.','The box was opened with a key.','The passive describes what happened to the box, while with identifies the instrument used.','The tool is not the human agent. Place with before the object that describes the instrument.'),
 G('gap','The report had been ___ before the meeting. Use write.','written','Had been written is past perfect passive, locating the completed writing before the past meeting.','The auxiliary group is complete. Supply the irregular participle rather than the past-simple form wrote.'),
 G('choice','Which sentence is a natural passive of “They let us leave”?','We were allowed to leave.','Allowed to leave expresses the permission in a natural passive, since let does not normally form this matching passive.','Do not mechanically form a passive with let. Choose the ordinary equivalent that keeps the permission meaning.',['We were allowed to leave.','We were let to leave.','We were allowed leave.']),
 G('edit','Correct the participle: The note was wrote in a hurry.','The note was written in a hurry.','Passive was requires the participle written, not the past-simple verb wrote.','The passive auxiliary is appropriate. Correct the irregular form of the main verb that follows it.'),
 G('rewrite','Start with She: They gave her a ticket.','She was given a ticket.','With give, the recipient can become the subject of a passive, followed by was given and the remaining object.','Move the recipient into subject form and keep the ticket as the remaining object after the passive verb.'),
 G('choice','Why might “My bag has been found” omit the finder?','The recovered bag matters more than who found it.','Passive voice can highlight a result when the agent is unknown, obvious or unimportant to the message.','Consider the purpose of the message to the traveller. An absent agent is not evidence that nobody performed the action.',['The recovered bag matters more than who found it.','A passive proves that no person found the bag.','Every passive forbids mentioning an agent.'])
];

 A('choice','What does the tag’s code allow the system to do?','Follow the bag through different journey stages.','The code supports tracking across the process rather than storing the owner’s complete travel history.','follow the bag through different stages of the journey.','Focus on what the code does as the bag moves.  A('choice','Which action belongs before leaving the airport?','Reporting the missing bag at the airline’s claim desk.','Olivia explicitly places the initial report before departure from the airport, not after reaching the hotel.','go to the airline’s claim desk before leaving the airport.','Pay attention to the time relationship.  A('gap','Staff ask for a baggage ___ as part of the report.','receipt','The receipt is one of the identifying items requested with the flight number and a description of the bag.','your baggage receipt, your flight number','The missing word names a document connected to checking the bag, rather than a physical feature of the suitcase.'),
 A('choice','Why do colour, brand and distinctive features matter?','They help staff recognise and match the suitcase.','Description details support identification when the tracking system and report are used to reconnect bag and passenger.','anything special that makes it easy to recognise.','Think about the purpose of the description, not merely a list of vocabulary for appearances.',['They help staff recognise and match the suitcase.','They decide which flight the passenger is allowed to take.','They guarantee that a suitcase can never be delayed.']),
 A('choice','What must happen for a found bag to be linked to the report?','The system must match the bag’s information with the report.','Finding the bag in another airport is followed by connecting that found item to the missing-bag record.','the system can match it with your report.','Distinguish locating a bag from identifying which passenger’s missing-bag report it belongs to.',['The system must match the bag’s information with the report.','The passenger must fly to every possible airport.','The airline must first replace all luggage tags.']),
 A('sequence','Order the claim process described by Olivia.',['The passenger reports the missing bag.','Staff collect documents and a description.','The airline creates a tracking report.','A found bag can be matched and returned.'],'The identifying information supports the report, which later helps connect a located bag to its owner.','After that, the airline creates a report.','Arrange the process stages rather than the reasons bags are delayed.  A('choice','What limit should a careful summary keep?','One or two days is common in the story, not a guarantee for every bag.','In many cases qualifies the return time; the recording does not promise a universal deadline.','In many cases, the suitcase is returned within one or two days','Notice the qualifying phrase before the return time. ];

'use strict';
const {C,G,A,V}=require('./lesson-authoring.cjs');
const cards=[
 C('Attribute a claim instead of presenting it as certain.','It is reported that the shop is changing.\nThe shop is reported to be changing.\n\nReporting passives put the information or topic first while attributing it to a report, belief or expectation.','Impersonal grammar is not evidence of truth. Identify the source where it matters, especially when reporting uncertain claims.'),
 C('Use it + reporting passive + clause.','It is said that the owner lives nearby.\nIt was thought that the shop would close.\nIt has been announced that classes will start.\n\nThe reporting verb’s tense shows when the saying, belief or announcement applies.','Keep a full subject and verb inside the that-clause. The report’s time can differ from the time of the reported event.'),
 C('Make the reported person or thing the subject.','The owner is believed to live nearby.\nThe team is expected to finish tomorrow.\n\nSubject + be + reporting participle + to-infinitive. Common verbs include say, believe, think, report and expect.','Not every verb accepts both patterns equally. It is suggested that… is useful, but do not freely create someone is suggested to… from it.'),
 C('Choose an infinitive for a simultaneous state or activity.','She is believed to own the shop. → current/general state\nThey are thought to be preparing an order. → activity in progress\n\nUse to + base or to be + -ing according to the reported meaning.','The activity may be simultaneous with a past report too: They were thought to be waiting. Match the relative timeline.'),
 C('Use a perfect infinitive for an earlier event.','She is said to have opened the shop in May.\nHe was believed to have left earlier.\nThey are reported to have been working all night.\n\nTo have + participle puts the event before the report; to have been + -ing highlights earlier activity.','The perfect infinitive does not make the reporting auxiliary past. Is said can introduce an event that happened long ago.'),
 C('Recognise useful variants.','There are said to be delays.\nShe is considered to be a skilled designer.\nCustomers are supposed to show a receipt.\n\nSupposed to may express an expectation or rule, not only an attributed belief.','Considered a skilled designer is also possible without to be. Avoid treating these variants as a single rigid conversion rule.'),
 C('Place a negative deliberately.','He is not believed to be abroad. → that belief is not held\nHe is believed not to be abroad. → the reported belief is negative\n\nThese can be close in everyday use but differ in emphasis and scope.','Use allegedly or reportedly to attribute carefully, not to hide an invented source. A passive report must remain faithful to what is known.'),
 C('Preserve the source and its limits.','Grace describes what happened to her family’s shop. A news-style summary can attribute those events to her account instead of inventing outside experts.\n\nRevisit the recording for evidence of the business changes.','The new questions separate actual events, reported opinions and unsupported interpretations. A more formal sentence is not automatically a more certain claim.')
];
const tasks=[
 G('choice','Which sentence correctly uses it + reporting passive?','It is believed that the shop is open.','The impersonal frame uses it, a passive reporting verb and a that-clause with its own subject and verb.','Look for a complete reporting frame followed by a full clause. Do not mix it-pattern and person-pattern structures.',['It is believed that the shop is open.','It is believed the shop to open.','The shop is believed that it is open.']),
 G('gap','The owner is said ___ live nearby. Complete the infinitive marker.','to','The subject-based reporting passive takes a to-infinitive after is said.','The owner is already the subject. Complete the reporting-passive pattern before the base verb live.'),
 G('order','Build a subject-based report of an activity in progress.','The team is thought to be preparing an order.','To be preparing gives the reported activity ongoing meaning relative to the current belief.','Keep is thought as the reporting passive. Use the progressive infinitive for the activity believed to be happening.'),
 G('edit','Correct the mixed patterns: They are said that they are abroad.','It is said that they are abroad.|They are said to be abroad.','Use either the it + that-clause frame or the subject + to-infinitive frame, rather than combining them.','There are two valid repairs. Choose one reporting frame and keep the information about their location unchanged.'),
 G('choice','Which infinitive places an event before the current report?','to have left','The perfect infinitive makes the leaving earlier than the reporting or belief, even if the report is current.','Look for the perfect auxiliary have after to. The simple or progressive forms do not by themselves mark the same earlier event.',['to have left','to leave','to be leaving']),
 G('gap','She is believed to have ___ the shop. Use open.','opened','To have opened is a perfect infinitive describing an opening that happened before the current belief.','Have needs a past participle. Keep the report current and complete only the form of the earlier event.'),
 G('choice','In “She was thought to be waiting”, what does was mark?','The time of the belief or report.','Was locates the reporting belief in the past, while to be waiting describes an activity at that reported time.','Separate the tense of thought from the aspect of waiting. The auxiliary in the reporting frame dates the belief.',['The time of the belief or report.','Proof that the waiting finished before the belief.','The date of a future waiting event.']),
 G('order','Build a report of an event earlier than the belief.','He is believed to have left yesterday.','Is believed is current reporting, while to have left puts the reported departure in the earlier past.','Keep the report’s auxiliary in the present. The perfect infinitive, not a past reporting auxiliary, dates the departure earlier.'),
 G('edit','Complete the infinitive: The prices are expected rise.','The prices are expected to rise.','Expected in this subject-based passive is followed by a to-infinitive, so to is required before rise.','The plural subject and passive auxiliary are already correct. Add the missing infinitive marker.'),
 G('gap','There ___ said to be delays. Use is or are.','are','There are said to be agrees with plural delays in this reporting-passive existence construction.','The reported things are plural. Choose the auxiliary that agrees with delays rather than the introductory there.'),
 G('choice','Which form describes an earlier ongoing activity?','They are reported to have been working.','To have been working is a perfect progressive infinitive, showing an earlier activity with duration or process focus.','Look for both the earlier-time perfect form and the progressive activity form after the reporting passive.',['They are reported to have been working.','They are reported to work tomorrow.','They are reported that working.']),
 G('rewrite','Use a subject-based reporting passive: People believe that Maya owns the shop.','Maya is believed to own the shop.','Maya becomes the subject, followed by is believed and a simple infinitive for the current ownership state.','Move the owner to subject position. Keep the ownership simultaneous with the belief rather than making it an earlier event.'),
 G('order','Build an impersonal report of a recent announcement.','It has been announced that the classes will start.','Has been announced dates the recent announcement; the that-clause retains the future start being announced.','Keep the reporting perfect passive together after it. The class start belongs inside a complete that-clause.'),
 G('gap','The shop is thought to ___ moving to a new building. Complete the progressive infinitive.','be','To be moving supplies the progressive infinitive after the reporting passive is thought.','Moving is an -ing form. Complete its progressive auxiliary without changing the current reporting frame.'),
 G('choice','Which statement about reporting passives is accurate?','They attribute a claim; they do not prove it true.','A reporting passive describes the status of information as reported or believed, rather than verifying the underlying event.','Separate the style of a sentence from the quality of its evidence. Formal attribution does not replace checking a source.',['They attribute a claim; they do not prove it true.','A passive report guarantees independent verification.','The phrase is believed means every source agrees.']),
 G('edit','Use the reliable it-pattern: The plan is suggested that we postpone it.','It is suggested that we postpone the plan.','Suggest naturally allows the impersonal it + that-clause frame here, avoiding an unsuitable mixed pattern.','Keep the suggestion’s meaning but use it as the introductory subject. Put the plan back into the reported clause.'),
 G('rewrite','Use a perfect infinitive: People say that she opened the shop last year.','She is said to have opened the shop last year.','The report is current, but the shop opening is earlier, so the subject-based passive needs a perfect infinitive.','Keep is said for the current report. Use the infinitive to locate the opening before now and retain the time phrase.'),
 G('choice','Which sentence places the negative inside the reported belief?','He is believed not to be abroad.','Not follows the reporting verb and negates the reported location, rather than negating the existence of the belief.','Check exactly where not appears. The question asks for a negative reported belief, not simply the absence of a positive belief.',['He is believed not to be abroad.','He is not believed to be abroad.','He is believed to be abroad.'])
];
const listening=[
 A('choice','Which information does Grace provide directly about the work?','Her uncle made most toys behind the shop.','The narrator identifies the uncle’s role and workshop location, giving a concrete source detail for a faithful summary.','My uncle made most of the toys in a small workshop behind the shop','Distinguish a stated role in Grace’s account from an inference about what an outside expert might have said.',['Her uncle made most toys behind the shop.','Outside experts certified every product that year.','The teacher bought the shop from the family.']),
 A('choice','How should a summary report the possible closure?','Her aunt said they might have to close.','The aunt expresses a possibility, not a completed closure or a promise that the business will remain open.','my aunt said they might have to close before the end of the year.','Preserve who voiced the concern and its uncertainty. Might have to close is not a report that closure already happened.',['Her aunt said they might have to close.','The shop had already closed permanently.','Her uncle guaranteed that costs would fall.']),
 A('choice','What did the teacher’s request suggest about demand?','Schools could be a useful audience for their products.','The request led to educational sets, providing a possible new audience rather than confirming a national contract.','create simple educational sets for schools.','Connect the customer’s request to the subsequent direction, but do not invent guaranteed orders beyond the account.',['Schools could be a useful audience for their products.','Every school had already signed a large order.','Local families were banned from buying the toys.']),
 A('gap','The new boxes included counting ___ alongside wooden letters.','pieces','Counting pieces are one of the specific contents Grace lists for the educational boxes.','wooden letters, counting pieces, small animals, and activity cards.','Use the exact product detail in the recording. Do not replace the contents with an invented educational item.'),
 A('choice','What did the videos demonstrate?','Ways children could learn and tell stories with the toys.','The videos showed practical uses of the products, helping the new direction reach people who valued those uses.','for learning and storytelling.','Focus on what was shown, rather than assuming the videos only advertised a discount or displayed manufacturing machinery.',['Ways children could learn and tell stories with the toys.','Instructions for reselling cheap plastic toys.','A promise that every child would learn at the same speed.']),
 A('choice','Which part of the transition required new skills?','Online orders, clearer descriptions and contact with schools.','Grace explicitly says they had to learn these tasks as part of reaching a different audience.','take online orders, write clearer descriptions, and speak to schools','Distinguish the existing craft skill from the additional communication and ordering skills needed for the new direction.',['Online orders, clearer descriptions and contact with schools.','Learning woodwork for the first time after decades in business.','Building a factory to replace every handmade product.']),
 A('sequence','Order evidence of the change in direction.',['A teacher identifies a classroom use for the toys.','The family starts making learning boxes.','Videos show ways to use the toys.','Teachers order boxes and customers share the videos.'],'The product idea develops before demonstration and later evidence of response from buyers.','Teachers ordered boxes for classrooms','Follow the steps that support the new direction. Do not place evidence of later demand before the products are introduced.'),
 A('choice','Which claim would go beyond Grace’s account?','Independent research proved the boxes improved every child’s results.','The account reports imagination, demand and survival, but does not report a universal independently measured learning result.','parents bought them as meaningful gifts','This question asks for an unsupported claim. Distinguish customer interest from evidence of guaranteed educational outcomes.',['Independent research proved the boxes improved every child’s results.','Parents bought the boxes as meaningful gifts.','The family changed how it described and sold its products.'])
];
const vocab=[V('attribution','identifying where information or a claim comes from','Reporting passives can do this, but the source must remain honest. The word concerns the origin of a statement, not proof it is true.'),V('account','a description of events given by someone','Grace supplies this about the family shop. In this lesson the noun means a narrative, not a bank balance or login.'),V('evidence','information that supports a conclusion','Orders and customer responses support the business’s changed direction. This word concerns support for a claim rather than confident wording.'),V('audience','the people a product or message is intended to reach','Schools become a new one for the toys. Here the word describes intended buyers and users, not only people watching a performance.'),V('survive','continue to exist despite difficulty','The family shop does this after changing direction. It means continuing through a challenge, not necessarily returning to its earlier size.'),V('assumption','something accepted as true without sufficient checking','A claim about guaranteed learning outcomes would be this if the account gave no supporting study. It differs from a stated fact.')];

'use strict';
const {C,G,A,V}=require('./lesson-authoring.cjs');
const cards=[
 C('Distinguish doing a job from arranging it.','I repaired the clock. → I did the work\nI had the clock repaired. → I arranged the repair\n\nHave + object + past participle focuses on a service someone else performs for us.','Do not assume that the subject performs the repair. Compare the whole verb pattern rather than just the past tense of have.'),
 C('Use get for an informal service arrangement.','She got her phone repaired.\nWe need to get the lock changed.\n\nGet + object + past participle is often less formal and can suggest effort or successful completion.','Have and get can both describe arranged services. Context, not the verb alone, establishes whether the task was difficult.'),
 C('Change have or get to locate the service in time.','I have the windows cleaned monthly.\nShe is having her car checked.\nWe had the roof repaired last week.\nI’ve had the brakes checked.\nWe’ll get the screen replaced tomorrow.','The participle describing the service remains the same. The tense belongs to have or get and any preceding auxiliaries.'),
 C('Ask questions with the right auxiliary.','Did you have your hair cut?\nWe don’t have our house painted yearly.\nHave you had the car checked?\n\nCausative have is a main verb. Do-support is used in simple-tense questions and negatives.','In Have you had…?, the first have is a perfect auxiliary; had is the causative main verb. They serve different jobs.'),
 C('Name the person doing the work if useful.','We had a mechanic check the brakes.\nWe got a mechanic to check the brakes.\n\nHave + person + base verb\nGet + person + to + base verb\n\nCompare: We had the brakes checked.','The object’s role determines the form. A mechanic performs the checking; the brakes receive it.'),
 C('Recognise an unwanted experience.','He had his wallet stolen.\nThey got their bikes damaged.\n\nThe same object + participle pattern can describe something bad happening to someone or their belongings, without their arranging it.','Do not interpret every have something done sentence as a chosen service. The event and context determine which meaning fits.'),
 C('Keep possession and other causatives clear.','I had my hair cut.\nShe got her coat cleaned.\nThe delay had us waiting for an hour.\n\nHave + person + -ing can describe keeping or causing someone in an ongoing situation.','Use possessives naturally with belongings and body parts. Avoid mixing get the car repaired with get a mechanic to repair the car.'),
 C('Arrange a service respectfully.','Adrian repairs clocks himself. A customer can arrange to have a clock repaired by him.\n\nRevisit the workshop recording for the skill, patience and personal value behind the service.','The new questions examine why repair matters to the people involved. Do not invent an agreed price, completion date or service promise absent from the recording.')
];
const tasks=[
 G('choice','Which sentence says the speaker arranged a repair by someone else?','I had my clock repaired.','Have + object + participle describes an arranged service here, unlike actively repairing the clock oneself.','Identify who is likely to perform the work from the whole pattern, not just from the subject I.',['I had my clock repaired.','I repaired my clock myself.','I was repairing my clock.']),
 G('gap','She got her phone ___. Use repair in the service pattern.','repaired','Get + object + past participle presents the phone as the receiver of the arranged service.','The phone receives the repair. Complete the participle after the object rather than adding an infinitive.'),
 G('order','Build a question about an arranged service in the past.','Did you have your hair cut?','Simple-past causative have uses did before the subject and the base form have, followed by object and participle.','Use did for the past question. Keep your hair as the receiver of the service and cut as the participle.'),
 G('edit','Correct the mixed pattern: I got my car to repaired.','I got my car repaired.','The car is the receiver, so get + object + participle requires repaired directly, with no to.','Do not use the person + to-infinitive pattern for the car receiving the work. Remove the extra marker.'),
 G('choice','Which sentence uses have + person + base verb?','We had a mechanic check the brakes.','A mechanic is the performer after have, so check is a bare infinitive in this causative pattern.','The object names the worker, not the repaired object. Choose the verb form that follows a person after causative have.',['We had a mechanic check the brakes.','We had a mechanic to check the brakes.','We had a mechanic checked the brakes.']),
 G('gap','We got a friend ___ design the poster. Complete the person pattern.','to','Get + person takes a to-infinitive, unlike have + person followed by a bare infinitive.','The friend performs the design. Complete the pattern for a person after got, not an object receiving a repair.'),

'use strict';
const {C,G,A,V}=require('./lesson-authoring.cjs');
const cards=[
 C('Connect a contrast without losing the meaning.','Although the library was old, it became popular again.\nEven though it was busy, a quiet room was available.\n\nAlthough/even though + subject + verb introduces a contrasting fact. Even though is often more emphatic.','Do not add a comma directly after although. An opening contrast clause normally takes a comma at its end.'),
 C('Use however as a sentence linker.','The building was old. However, its purpose was changing.\nThe room was small; nevertheless, it was useful.\n\nHowever, nevertheless and nonetheless can connect contrasting statements across a full stop or semicolon.','Avoid joining two complete clauses with only a comma before however. Sentence-final though is common in speech: It was useful, though.'),
 C('Use a noun or -ing after despite.','Despite the noise, we studied.\nIn spite of arriving early, we missed the start.\nDespite the fact that it was raining, we went.\n\nDespite has no of; in spite of keeps of.','The example needs a genuinely surprising contrast. Arriving early but missing the start works if another delay or problem intervenes.'),
 C('Compare facts or allow a possibility.','My brother likes cafés, whereas I prefer libraries.\nEven though it is raining, we will go. → rain is a fact\nEven if it rains, we will go. → rain is a possibility\n\nWhile can also compare facts as well as describe simultaneous actions.','Choose even if or even though for the intended reality, not merely because both are followed by a clause.'),
 C('Explain an action’s purpose with an infinitive.','They opened a quiet room to help students focus.\nWe stayed late in order to finish.\nShe wrote it down so as not to forget.\n\nTo + base verb is common; in order to / so as to can be more explicit or formal.','Negative purpose commonly uses in order not to or so as not to. Do not use for to as the infinitive marker.'),
 C('Use so that with a complete clause.','They made a quiet area so that students could concentrate.\nClose the door so that the noise won’t disturb us.\n\nSo that can introduce a purpose with its own subject and often a modal.','Compare result: It was noisy, so we left. Purpose describes an intended outcome; result describes what follows.'),
 C('Distinguish a specific aim from general function.','We stopped for a coffee. → for + noun\nThis room is for recording podcasts. → function\nI came to record a podcast. → my purpose\n\nFor + -ing is useful for general function, but an action’s specific purpose normally uses a to-infinitive.','Keep the subject and relationship clear. A room for visitors to study names a space intended for other people’s action.'),
 C('Make a balanced practical proposal.','Noah’s library expanded its activities without losing quiet reading. Revisit the recording to identify the different needs and the reasons for the changes.\n\nUse contrast to acknowledge a constraint and purpose to explain a proposed response.','Connect each goal to a practical choice. Explain how a change can help one group while preserving a useful benefit for others.')
];
const tasks=[
 G('choice','Which sentence uses although with a complete clause?','Although the room was small, it was useful.','Although introduces a subject and finite verb, followed by the contrasting main clause.','Look for a complete clause after although, rather than a noun phrase that would fit despite.',['Although the room was small, it was useful.','Although the small room, it was useful.','Although of the room was small, it was useful.']),
 G('gap','___ the noise, we finished the task. Use despite or although.','Despite','Despite can introduce the noun phrase the noise, whereas although normally introduces a full clause.','Check the structure following the gap. It is a noun phrase, with no subject-and-verb clause of its own.'),
 G('order','Build an opening clause of factual contrast.','Even though it was busy, we found a quiet room.','Even though presents the busy situation as a fact, contrasting with the successful search for a quiet room.','Keep the factual contrast clause first and the main outcome second. The clause boundary needs the supplied comma.'),
 G('edit','Correct the linker: Despite of the rain, we went out.','Despite the rain, we went out.|In spite of the rain, we went out.','Use despite without of, or the complete expression in spite of, before the noun phrase.','There are two valid repairs. Keep the contrast and use one complete prepositional expression.'),
 G('choice','Which sentence punctuates however naturally between full statements?','It was noisy. However, we stayed.','A full stop separates the complete statements; however then introduces the contrast and is followed by a comma.','Both parts are complete clauses. Choose punctuation that separates them before using the sentence linker.',['It was noisy. However, we stayed.','It was noisy, however we stayed.','It was noisy however, we stayed.']),
 G('gap','We came ___ borrow some books. Use to or for.','to','To borrow describes the purpose of this particular visit, using a to-infinitive rather than for + base verb.','The following word is a base verb describing the aim of the visit, not a noun or general-function -ing form.'),
 G('choice','Which sentence leaves rain as a possibility rather than asserting it as fact?','Even if it rains, we will go.','Even if introduces a possible condition that does not change the intended decision to go.','Compare a possible future condition with a known contrasting fact. The question asks for the possibility.',['Even if it rains, we will go.','Even though it is raining, we will go.','It is raining, but we will go.']),
 G('order','Build a purpose clause with a different subject.','They made a quiet room so that students could study.','So that introduces the students’ intended action, using its own subject and the modal could.','Keep the room-making action first. The people benefiting from it become the subject inside the purpose clause.'),
 G('edit','Correct the specific-purpose infinitive: I came for to ask a question.','I came to ask a question.','A to-infinitive expresses the specific purpose of coming; for to is not the standard marker here.','The question asks why the speaker came. Remove the extra preposition before the infinitive marker.'),
 G('gap','She wrote a reminder so as ___ to forget. Complete the negative purpose.','not','So as not to forget gives the negative intended outcome, placing not before the infinitive marker.','The purpose is preventing forgetting. Complete the negative expression between so as and to.'),
 G('choice','Which sentence describes a room’s general function?','This room is for recording podcasts.','For + -ing describes the room’s intended use, rather than the purpose of a particular person’s visit.','Look for the function of an object or space. A specific action such as I came normally uses a to-infinitive.',['This room is for recording podcasts.','I came for record a podcast.','This room is so that recording podcasts.']),
 G('rewrite','Use although: Despite the rain, we went out.','Although it was raining, we went out.|Although it rained, we went out.','Changing from despite to although requires a complete clause expressing the same rainy condition.','Replace the noun phrase with a subject-and-verb clause. Both a past state in progress and the simple past can fit.'),
 G('order','Build a comparison between two preferences.','My brother likes cafés, whereas I prefer libraries.','Whereas links contrasting facts with separate subjects, without introducing a purpose or an uncertain condition.','Keep each person with their own preference. Put the comparison linker between the two complete clauses.'),
 G('gap','In spite ___ arriving early, we missed the start. Complete the fixed expression.','of','In spite of takes a noun or -ing phrase, so of completes the expression before arriving.','This is the three-word expression contrasting with despite. Retain the supplied -ing phrase after it.'),
 G('choice','Which sentence gives a result rather than a purpose?','It was noisy, so we left.','Leaving is presented as the consequence of the noise, not as the intended aim of making noise.','Ask whether the second clause explains an intention or what happened as a consequence. The question asks for a consequence.',['It was noisy, so we left.','We closed the door so that we could study.','They moved the chairs to create space.']),
 G('edit','Correct the opening punctuation: Although, it was late we continued.','Although it was late, we continued.','There is no comma immediately after although; the comma normally comes at the end of the opening contrast clause.','Find the boundary between the two clauses. The comma belongs there rather than directly after the linker.'),
 G('rewrite','Use in order to: We stayed late to finish the work.','We stayed late in order to finish the work.','In order to makes the same intended purpose more explicit while preserving the subject and action.','Replace the short infinitive marker with the longer purpose expression without changing the rest of the action.'),
 G('choice','Which proposal connects a constraint with a useful purpose?','Although space is limited, we can divide it to support quiet study.','Although acknowledges a real constraint, while to support explains the aim of the suggested response.','Choose a coherent contrast and purpose that could guide an actual decision, rather than merely collecting linkers.',['Although space is limited, we can divide it to support quiet study.','Despite we space, however to quiet study.','We divide the space although for to because.'])
];
const listening=[
 A('choice','What contrast frames Noah’s return visit?','The familiar building has a very different social energy.','The building remains recognisable, while the mix of active users makes it feel transformed.','the same building, but with a completely different energy.','Compare continuity in the building with change in how people use it. The story does not describe a newly built replacement library.',['The familiar building has a very different social energy.','The library has moved entirely online and the building is closed.','The building is new but no one uses it.']),
 A('choice','Why did the library avoid competing directly with the internet?','It focused on a calm space, helpful people and local community.','The librarian identifies human and local benefits as its direction, rather than trying to replace online information.','a calm space, helpful people, and a real local community.','Identify the positive alternative the library offered, not only the competitor it chose not to imitate.',['It focused on a calm space, helpful people and local community.','It planned to remove every digital resource.','It promised to contain every fact available online.']),
 A('gap','Teenagers were recording a ___ in the glass room.','podcast','The recording activity illustrates one new use alongside studying, children’s visits and computer access.','teenagers recording a podcast in a glass room','The missing word is the audio activity Noah notices on his return, not the type of club mentioned later.'),
 A('choice','How did separate areas help the new approach?','They allowed different needs to be served within the same building.','The quiet room, children’s corner, digital area and event space let the library accommodate different purposes.','different areas for different needs.','Connect the physical layout to the variety of visitors. The new activities did not require every area to become noisy.',['They allowed different needs to be served within the same building.','They removed quiet study from the building completely.','They gave every visitor the same task at the same time.']),
 A('choice','Which contribution came from retired teachers?','Help with homework.','Retired teachers contributed a skill to local students, alongside artists displaying work and clubs meeting.','Retired teachers helped students with homework.','Keep each community contributor with the activity Noah actually assigns to them, rather than mixing the roles.',['Help with homework.','Replacing all librarians with volunteers.','Recording every teenager’s podcast.']),
 A('gap','One practical workshop taught people how to write a ___.','CV|cv','Writing a CV is among the practical workshop topics, alongside online services, family research and recording audio.','how to write a CV','The question asks for the job-related document in the workshop list, not the books borrowed by visitors.'),
 A('sequence','Order the development Noah describes.',['The library chooses benefits it can offer beyond online information.','It creates areas for different needs.','It adds practical workshops.','Local people contribute art, help and club activities.'],'The strategic choice is followed by changes to space, organised learning and wider community participation.','First, they created different areas','Follow the development in the librarian’s explanation, not the order in which Noah first noticed individual visitors.'),
 A('choice','What made the change balanced rather than a loss of purpose?','New activities were added while books and quiet reading remained.','The expanded uses gave more reasons to visit without removing the original reading and help functions.','the library did not lose its original purpose.','Use the final qualification. Popularity did not mean replacing reading with entertainment throughout the building.',['New activities were added while books and quiet reading remained.','Every book was removed so that events could occupy all the rooms.','Quiet reading was allowed only outside the library.'])
];
const vocab=[V('flexible','able to adapt to different needs or situations','The library serves more purposes while preserving quiet areas. This word concerns adaptability rather than being physically soft.'),V('resource','something useful that supports an activity or learning','The library offers digital examples as well as books and people. A resource is something usable, not only a piece of technology.'),V('participation','taking part in an activity','Local people contribute more than borrowing books. This noun describes active involvement rather than simply being nearby.'),V('constraint','a limit that affects what can be done','Limited space is one in a practical proposal. It names a boundary to work with, not necessarily a reason to abandon the project.'),V('preserve','keep something valuable while preventing its loss','The library retains quiet reading as it changes. This verb concerns keeping an existing benefit rather than replacing everything.'),V('purpose','the aim or intended function of something','The lesson contrasts this with a result that happens afterwards. It explains what an action or space is intended to achieve.')];

Keep quiet users and other users in mind.',speaking:'For 60–90 seconds, discuss improvements to a shared space with another user. 'use strict';
const {C,G,A,V}=require('./lesson-authoring.cjs');
const cards=[
 C('Leave a choice open.','Take whatever you need.\nSit wherever you like.\nCall whenever you are free.\n\nThese clauses allow an unspecified choice of thing, place or time. In other contexts they mean no matter what/where/when.','Read the relationship in the whole sentence. Whoever answers first gets the call is a description of a person, not permission to do anything at all.'),
 C('Choose whatever or whichever.','Bring whatever equipment helps. → open choice\nTake whichever of these two routes is clearer. → a defined set\n\nWhatever and whichever can stand alone or introduce a noun phrase. Whichever often points to a limited selection.','Use whichever of before a specified plural group. Do not keep question inversion inside a clause such as choose whichever route you prefer.'),
 C('Use whoever to identify a person.','Whoever calls first will get help.\nWe will support whoever needs training.\n\nThe clause can be a sentence’s subject or object. When whoever is its own clause’s subject, keep the normal verb after it.','A subject clause stays joined to its predicate: Whoever calls first gets help. Do not put a comma between that whole subject and gets.'),
 C('Specify any time or place.','You can work wherever you feel comfortable.\nWhenever you arrive, send a message.\n\nAn opening time/place clause normally takes a comma. A following integrated clause usually does not.','Compare a clause that gives the main action’s time with a clause serving as the whole subject. Not every opening -ever clause needs a comma.'),
 C('Use however for manner or degree.','Arrange the notes however you like. → in any way\nHowever difficult it is, try one step. → no matter how difficult\n\nPut the adjective or adverb directly after however in the degree pattern.','Do not confuse this with the sentence linker However, we continued.  C('Keep quantity and duration clear.','However many bags you bring, label them.\nHowever much time it takes, check carefully.\nWait however long you need.\n\nMany goes with countable plurals; much with uncountable amounts.','Long and far can describe duration and distance. Keep the verb and subject in ordinary clause order.'),
 C('Give advice that applies across choices.','Whatever happens, keep your ticket.\nWhichever train you choose, check the platform.\nWherever possible, save a backup.\n\nAn opening no-matter clause can establish that the advice applies regardless of the choice or event.','Use a present form for ordinary future time clauses: Whenever you arrive, call. A different sentence may contain an embedded question with will.'),
 C('Make a flexible backup plan.','Daniel had a careful plan, but a cancellation required new decisions. Revisit his journey with new questions about information, uncertainty and adaptation.','Keep the actual story distinct from your advice. Use -ever clauses to give practical guidance that remains useful when details change.')
];

 G('choice','Which sentence leaves the place of work open?','Work wherever you feel comfortable.','Wherever introduces the unspecified place where the person may choose to work.','Look for the place word rather than the time or person word.  G('gap','Choose ___ of these two routes you prefer.  G('order','Build advice that applies regardless of what happens.','Whatever happens, keep your ticket.','Whatever happens establishes that the instruction applies across possible events, with a comma after the opening clause.','Keep the no-matter clause first.  G('edit','Correct the embedded order: Choose whichever route do you prefer.','Choose whichever route you prefer.','The choice clause uses subject + verb order, so the question auxiliary do is not needed.','This is an instruction containing a choice clause, not a direct question.  G('choice','Which sentence correctly uses a clause as its subject?','Whoever calls first gets help.','The whole whoever-clause is the subject of gets help and is not separated from that predicate by a comma.','Identify the whole subject, not just the opening word.  G('rewrite','Use wherever: Sit in any place you like.','Sit wherever you like.','Wherever introduces the unspecified place and replaces the longer any-place expression.','Keep the instruction sit and the freedom to choose a place. Use the place -ever word with normal clause order.'),

 G('edit','Correct the degree pattern: However it is difficult, try one step.','However difficult it is, try one step.','In the concessive degree pattern, however is followed directly by the adjective, then subject and verb.','Move the adjective next to however while preserving the subject and linking verb inside the opening clause.'),
 G('rewrite','Use however much: No matter how much time it takes, check carefully.','However much time it takes, check carefully.','However much time expresses the same no-matter-the-amount meaning with an uncountable noun.','Replace the opening no-matter expression, keep the amount noun time, and preserve the practical instruction.'),
 G('choice','Why is there no comma in “Take whatever you need”?','The whatever-clause is the object of take.','The integrated object clause completes the verb’s meaning and is not an opening supplementary instruction clause.','Think about the job of the clause. 'use strict';
const {C,G,A,V}=require('./lesson-authoring.cjs');
const cards=[
 C('Distinguish a general group from a specified group.','Most people want useful choices.\nMost of the people in this group chose tea.\nMost of us agreed.\n\nUse most + noun for a general group; most of + the/my/these or an object pronoun for a specified one.','Do not put of directly before a bare general plural: most of people needs either most people or most of the people.'),
 C('Use all with the right structure.','All students need time.\nAll (of) the students arrived.\nAll of them were ready.\nWe have all finished.\n\nAll can stand alone when its reference is clear: All were welcome. Everybody is often clearer without that context.','All of is required before object pronouns. Mid-position all commonly follows the first auxiliary, as in have all finished.'),
 C('Use both for a pair.','Both cafés are open.\nBoth of them serve tea.\nThey were both busy.\n\nBoth refers to two and takes plural agreement. Both A and B links the two members.','Not both means at least one fails the condition; neither means both fail it. Avoid an ambiguous both…not sentence when the distinction matters.'),
 C('Use either or neither for two options.','Either café is fine. → one or the other\nNeither café is open. → not one and not the other\n\nEither/neither + singular noun normally takes a singular verb. Either/neither of takes a specified plural group.','After either/neither of + plural, singular agreement is common in careful writing and plural occurs in speech. Do not reject every plural form automatically.'),
 C('Choose no or none.','There is no milk.\nWe have no tickets.\nHow many tickets? None.\nNone of the tickets are left.\n\nNo comes before a noun; none stands alone or takes of + a specified group.','With none of + plural, singular or plural agreement can fit. With an uncountable noun, use singular: None of the water is clean.'),
 C('Use any for absence or an open choice.','Do you have any questions?\nWe don’t have any milk.\nChoose any seat.\n\nAny can be used in questions, negatives and affirmative open-choice statements.','The meaning depends on the sentence. Some is also natural in offers and requests when a positive answer is expected.'),
 C('Keep number, scope and agreement together.','All the bread is fresh. → uncountable singular\nBoth options are useful. → two, plural\nNeither option is available. → two, neither one\nNot all options are useful. → less than all, not necessarily none','Check what the negative covers before choosing a quantifier. Not all and none do not express the same quantity.'),
 C('Describe choices accurately.','Lena describes a large range of products and the effort of choosing. Revisit her supermarket visit with new questions about quantity, scope and her final strategy.','Avoid turning some people’s routines into a claim about everybody. In your own plan, say which group or pair you actually mean.')
];
const tasks=[
 G('choice','Which sentence describes people generally?','Most people appreciate clear options.','Most followed by a bare plural noun makes a general statement rather than specifying one already identified group.','Compare the general group with the version containing of the. The question asks about people in general.',['Most people appreciate clear options.','Most of the people in our group chose tea.','Most of us chose tea.']),
 G('gap','Most ___ the students in this class agreed. Complete the specific-group pattern.','of','Most of introduces the specified group the students in this class, rather than a general bare plural.','The group is explicitly identified by the and in this class. Add the connector needed after most.'),
 G('order','Build a sentence with mid-position all.','We have all finished the task.','All can follow the first auxiliary have, referring back to the plural subject we.','Keep the perfect auxiliary before all and the main participle after it. The group is already identified by we.'),
 G('edit','Correct the pronoun pattern: All them were ready.','All of them were ready.','All of is needed before the object pronoun them when naming the entire specified group.','The reference is an object pronoun rather than a noun with a determiner. Complete the phrase before them.'),
 G('choice','Which sentence correctly refers to two places with both?','Both cafés are open.','Both takes a plural noun and plural agreement when it refers to the two members of a pair.','The question asks for both members of a pair. Check that the following noun and verb agree with that meaning.',['Both cafés are open.','Both café is open.','Both cafés is open.']),
 G('gap','Neither option ___ available. Use is or are in careful standard agreement.','is','Neither followed directly by a singular noun uses singular agreement, unlike a plural subject with both.','The noun is singular option, not a plural of-phrase. Use the ordinary singular agreement for this pattern.'),
 G('choice','What does “Not both options are available” establish?','At least one option is unavailable.','Not both denies that the pair are both available, without necessarily saying that neither is available.','Read the scope of not. It rules out both being available but leaves open whether one or no options are available.',['At least one option is unavailable.','Neither option is available in every possible case.','Both options are definitely available.']),
 G('order','Build a statement of absence with no before a noun.','We have no time to compare everything.','No directly modifies the uncountable noun time, giving an affirmative verb phrase with negative meaning.','Keep no next to the noun it modifies. None cannot be placed directly before time in the same pattern.'),
 G('edit','Correct the general-group pattern: Most of people want a choice.','Most people want a choice.','Most directly modifies a bare plural for a general reference; of would need an identified group such as the people.','The sentence concerns people generally. Remove the connector that would require a specific determiner or pronoun.'),
 G('gap','How many tickets are left? ___. Use no or none as a complete reply.','None','None can stand alone as a pronoun meaning not any, while no normally needs a following noun in this use.','The reply contains no following noun. Choose the pronoun that can provide the complete answer.'),
 G('choice','Which sentence permits any single member of an open set?','Choose any seat.','Any in this affirmative instruction means that no particular seat is required; any available choice is acceptable.','Do not assume any can appear only in negatives. Look for a sentence allowing an unrestricted choice.',['Choose any seat.','No seat is available.','Neither of the two seats is free.']),
 G('rewrite','Use neither: Both cafés are closed.','Neither café is open.','If both cafés are closed, neither of the pair is open; the singular noun café takes is.','Change from both being closed to neither being open. Preserve the meaning and use a singular noun after neither.'),
 G('order','Build a specific-group statement with an object pronoun.','Most of us preferred the simpler option.','Most of us identifies a portion of the speaker’s group, using of before the object pronoun.','Keep most of us together as the subject. The past verb then describes that group’s preference.'),
 G('gap','None of the water ___ clean. Use is or are.','is','Water is uncountable here, so the none of phrase takes singular agreement in this sentence.','Check the noun water. Agreement possibilities with a countable plural do not make this uncountable noun plural.'),
 G('choice','Which statement about “All were welcome” is accurate?','It can be grammatical when the group is clear.','All may stand alone with an understood reference; everybody or all the visitors can be clearer without that context.','Avoid an absolute ban on a pronoun use. Consider whether the preceding context identifies the people meant.',['It can be grammatical when the group is clear.','It is impossible in every variety of standard English.','It always refers to exactly two people.']),
 G('edit','Correct the ordinary negative: We don’t have no milk.','We don’t have any milk.|We have no milk.','Use a negative verb with any, or an affirmative verb with no, to express the intended absence in standard English.','Preserve the single negative meaning. Either replace the determiner or remove the negative auxiliary.'),
 G('rewrite','Use both of + pronoun: The two of them agreed.','Both of them agreed.','Both of them refers to the specified pair and keeps the plural subject’s agreement with agreed.','Keep the reference to the same two people. Use the quantifier of the pair before the supplied object pronoun.'),
 G('choice','Which contrast correctly distinguishes scope?','Not all agreed may mean some agreed; none agreed means zero.','Not all only rules out complete agreement, while none states that there was no agreement from anyone in the group.','Check how many the negative excludes. Less than all is not automatically the same as zero.',['Not all agreed may mean some agreed; none agreed means zero.','Not all agreed and none agreed always mean exactly the same.','None agreed necessarily means every person agreed.'])
];
const listening=[
 A('choice','How does Lena’s actual visit compare with her expectation?','A short errand becomes a much longer comparison of products.','She expected ten minutes but spent almost half an hour at the shelves considering choices she did not care much about.','comparing products I did not really care about.','Compare the intended simple purchase with the activity that absorbed her time, rather than only counting the products.',['A short errand becomes a much longer comparison of products.','A long planned visit ends before she reaches any shelf.','She spends the visit collecting a pre-ordered box at the entrance.']),
 A('choice','Why do similar-looking cereal brands matter in the example?','They add options without making the differences easy to judge.','The list includes several brands that looked almost the same, increasing comparison effort rather than removing it.','several brands that looked almost the same.','Connect the appearance of similar choices to the effort of selecting, not to an invented claim that all cereals taste identical.',['They add options without making the differences easy to judge.','They prove that every brand contains exactly the same ingredients.','They make the supermarket remove every other breakfast product.']),
 A('gap','At first Lena expected the shopping to take ___ minutes.','10|ten','The initial ten-minute expectation contrasts with the almost half-hour comparison she later describes.','I expected to be there for ten minutes.','The number concerns her original expectation. Keep it distinct from the later time limit she uses for small decisions.'),
 A('choice','What happens to the feeling of freedom as comparison continues?','It gives way to tiredness.','Lena initially welcomes being able to choose exactly what she wants, then finds the continuing comparison exhausting.','stopped feeling free and started feeling tired.','Track the change in her reaction, rather than assuming her first positive response remains unchanged throughout the visit.',['It gives way to tiredness.','It grows into certainty that she has found a perfect product.','It makes her finish every future decision instantly.']),
 A('choice','Which concern makes each extra option mentally costly?','The possibility of regretting a different choice.','Lena describes imagined mistakes and the fear that a better alternative might exist elsewhere.','Will I regret not choosing the other one?','Listen for the question behind repeated comparison. The concern is about a possible alternative, not just the visible price.' ,['The possibility of regretting a different choice.','A rule that customers must buy every brand.','Proof that the first option is always unsafe.']),
 A('choice','Why do some people simplify routine choices?','To save attention for more important decisions.','Time and energy spent on small decisions can leave people mentally tired when a more important decision appears.','when we need to make an important decision, we may feel mentally tired.','Connect the small routine simplifications to the later need for attention. Do not turn some people into all people.',['To save attention for more important decisions.','Because nobody values personal choice at all.','Because every small decision has the same importance as a major one.']),
 A('sequence','Order the changes in Lena’s view.',['A large range first seems helpful.','Continued comparison starts to feel tiring.','She considers the cost of worrying about better alternatives.','She adopts a brief limit for small decisions.'],'The story develops from initial enthusiasm to decision costs and a practical strategy for less important choices.','I now give myself a short time limit.','Follow the development of the argument. Her later strategy comes after recognising the burden of too much comparison.'),
 A('choice','What limit does Lena place on her own strategy?','She applies the short time limit to small decisions.','The strategy is introduced specifically for small decisions, rather than a rule to rush every major life choice.','For small decisions, I now give myself a short time limit.','Preserve the scope of the advice. A strategy for a box of cereal is not automatically a rule for every important decision.',['She applies the short time limit to small decisions.','She says every important decision must be finished in two minutes.','She removes choice completely from everyone’s daily life.'])
];

'use strict';
const {C,G,A,V}=require('./lesson-authoring.cjs');
const cards=[
 C('Describe an impression with an adjective.','The café looks welcoming.\nThe music sounds quiet.\nThe chair feels soft.\nThe soup tastes good.\nThe bread smells fresh.\n\nThese linking uses describe the subject rather than how someone performs an action.','Use an adjective as the complement. Degree adverbs can still modify it: It sounds really interesting.'),
 C('Recognise an action use.','The soup tastes salty. → its quality\nShe tasted the soup carefully. → an action\nHe looked tired. → his appearance\nHe looked at the label carefully. → deliberate looking','An adverb can describe how an action is performed. Do not apply the adjective-complement rule to every use of the same verb.'),
 C('Compare with like + noun.','It smells like coffee.\nYou sound like your brother.\nThe fabric feels like silk.\n\nLike introduces the thing or person used for comparison. A direct adjective does not need like: It feels soft.','A resemblance is not proof of identity or ingredients. Something tasting like nuts does not establish exactly what it contains.'),
 C('Use as if or as though with a clause.','It looks as if someone has moved the chairs.\nShe sounds as though she is tired.\nHe acts as if he owned the place.\n\nChoose the tense for the apparent time and whether the situation is treated as real, uncertain or unreal.','A past form can mark distance from reality, but is not compulsory after every as if. Do not change a plausible present impression to past automatically.'),
 C('Notice spoken and descriptive alternatives.','It looks like it is going to rain. → informal like + clause\nThe room smells of coffee. → a coffee smell\nYou look well. → healthy\n\nTaste/smell of describes a characteristic flavour or smell; like emphasises similarity.','A smell alone does not confirm ingredients or a safe condition. Well can be an adjective meaning healthy, so it is not always an incorrect complement.'),
 C('Distinguish an impression from a wish.','The plan sounds practical. → impression\nI feel like staying here. → desire\nIt seems possible. → judgement\n\nFeel like + -ing means wanting to do something, rather than describing a texture.','Seem and appear also take adjective complements. Keep the intended meaning clear before choosing the following form.'),
 C('Explain whose impression it is.','The café sounds familiar to me.\nTo me, the room feels calm.\nThe drink tastes a little bitter.\n\nA phrase such as to me can identify the observer. A degree word can soften the description.','An impression can be personal and incomplete. Explain the evidence rather than presenting every observation as a confirmed fact.'),
 C('Describe a place beyond its products.','Emma describes how attention and small details change the feel of a café. Revisit her account with new questions about experience, atmosphere and exceptions.','Use the senses and impressions to describe your own place. Keep the talk’s qualification that neither smallness nor size alone guarantees a personal experience.')
];
const tasks=[
 G('choice','Which sentence describes the soup’s quality with a linking verb?','The soup tastes salty.','Tastes links the soup to the adjective salty, describing a quality rather than an action done carefully.','Identify the subject being described. The question asks about the soup’s quality, not the manner of tasting it.',['The soup tastes salty.','She tasted the soup carefully.','She looked at the soup quietly.']),
 G('gap','The room smells ___. Use fresh or freshly as the complement.','fresh','The linking verb smells takes the adjective fresh to describe the room’s apparent quality.','The missing word describes the room itself. Choose an adjective rather than an adverb describing how a person acts.'),
 G('order','Build a comparison with a noun after like.','The fabric feels like silk.','Feels like introduces silk as the material used for comparison, without proving that it is genuine silk.','Keep like directly before the comparison noun.  G('edit','Correct the adjective complement: The music sounds beautifully.','The music sounds beautiful.','Sounds links the subject music to an adjective describing its perceived quality, so beautiful is appropriate.','The music is being evaluated, not performing a listening action.  G('choice','Which sentence uses a sense verb as a deliberate action?','She smelled the milk carefully.','The subject actively checks the milk, and carefully describes how she performs that action.','Look for a person carrying out a check on an object.  G('gap','You sound ___ your mother.  G('choice','Which sentence keeps a plausible current impression in the present?','She sounds as though she is tired.','A present clause is natural for an impression of current tiredness; past forms are not required after every as though.','Do not mechanically backshift every impression clause.  G('order','Build a personal impression with a degree modifier.','The café sounds really welcoming to me.','Really modifies the adjective welcoming, while to me identifies whose impression is being expressed.','Keep the degree word next to the adjective.  G('edit','Correct the action phrase: He listened the announcement carefully.','He listened to the announcement carefully.','The deliberate action listen normally takes to before its object, unlike a linking verb such as sound.','The announcement is the thing being deliberately heard.  G('gap','I feel like ___ here for a while. Use stay.','staying','Feel like followed by -ing expresses a desire to do the activity rather than a sensory comparison to a noun.','This speaker expresses what they want to do. Use the activity form after the preposition like in this expression.'),
 G('choice','What can “You look well” mean?','You appear healthy.','Well can be an adjective meaning in good health, so this is a valid linking-verb description.','Remember the health meaning of well.  G('rewrite','Use sounds + adjective: My impression is that the plan is practical.','The plan sounds practical.','Sounds practical presents the plan’s apparent quality through a linking verb and an adjective complement.','Make the plan the subject and retain the judgement as an impression, using the requested linking verb.'),
 G('order','Build an impression supported by an apparent earlier event.','It looks as if someone has moved the chairs.','The present impression is linked to an apparently completed action through the present-perfect clause.','Keep as if together before the clause. The action has a current visible result, so keep has with the participle.'),
 G('gap','The bread smells ___ garlic. Complete its preposition before the noun.'),
 G('choice','Which statement about “It tastes like peanuts” is careful?','It describes a resemblance, not confirmed ingredients.','Like reports similarity in taste; determining actual ingredients requires information beyond that impression.','Keep the sensory comparison separate from a claim about exactly what is inside the food.',['It describes a resemblance, not confirmed ingredients.','It proves the food contains only peanuts.','It guarantees the food is suitable for every eater.']),
 G('edit','Correct the linking complement: The chair feels comfortably.','The chair feels comfortable.','Feels describes the chair through an adjective complement, rather than the manner of an action performed by the chair.','The chair is the thing evaluated by touch or use.  G('rewrite','Use look + adjective: They appear tired.','They look tired.','Look can link the plural subject to the adjective tired, describing appearance rather than deliberate observation.','Keep the description of the people’s appearance. Use look directly before the same adjective.'),
 G('choice','Which contrast separates linking and action uses?','He looked happy. / He looked at the label carefully.','The first evaluates the subject’s appearance; the second describes deliberate looking with an object and manner adverb.','Compare what follows looked. An adjective describes the person; at plus an object identifies the target of an action.',['He looked happy. / He looked at the label carefully.','He looked happily person. / He looked at happy.','He looked happiness. / He looked the label without at.'])
];

 A('choice','What does Emma’s change of view add to the idea of a café?','It can offer recognition and company as well as a drink.','Her opening moves from coffee as the main purpose to a wider emotional and social experience.','feel noticed, relaxed, and a little less alone.','Connect the opening change of opinion with the experience described later, rather than reducing the argument to drink quality.',['It can offer recognition and company as well as a drink.','It is useful only if it sells expensive coffee.','Its main purpose is to replace every home kitchen.']),

 A('choice','What changes when Emma becomes a regular?','She feels recognised as a person rather than only another order.','The owner’s memory and attention create a relationship that changes the atmosphere for Emma.','I was not just another customer in a queue.','Look beyond the label regular customer to the effect of being remembered.  A('choice','Which benefit does Emma still allow for chain cafés?','Speed and predictability can suit someone in a hurry.','She acknowledges their convenience while discussing why some experiences can feel anonymous.','If you are in a hurry, that can be perfect.','Preserve the positive part of her comparison.  A('choice','Why can mismatched chairs fit the positive description?','Small imperfections may contribute to a warmer atmosphere.','Emma describes the simple menu and mismatched furniture as part of the warmth rather than automatic defects.','these imperfections often make the place warmer.','Interpret warmer in the social atmosphere, not only as a physical temperature measurement inside the room.',['Small imperfections may contribute to a warmer atmosphere.','The chairs prove the building has a broken heating system.','Every mismatch guarantees excellent service.']),
 A('sequence','Order the development of Emma’s personal example.',['She moves into a neighbourhood where she knows nobody.','She first visits a nearby café for its location.','The owner remembers her name and preferences.','The café becomes part of her routine and community.'],'The example moves from a new unfamiliar area to repeated contact and a sense of local connection.','It became part of my routine','Follow the story of becoming familiar with a place rather than arranging the general café comparison as a list of facts.'),
 A('choice','Which qualification prevents an overgeneralisation about size?','Not every small café is special, and not every chain café is cold.','Emma says attention, rather than size alone, is central to the personal feeling she describes.','The difference is not only about size.','Keep the explicit exception in mind. ];
const vocab=[V('welcoming','making people feel accepted and comfortable','This can describe a café’s atmosphere with a linking verb. Here it concerns the social feeling rather than the scientific layers of air around Earth.'),V('imperfection','a small feature that falls short of an ideal standard','Mismatched chairs illustrate one in the talk. 'use strict';
const {C,G,A,V}=require('./lesson-authoring.cjs');
const cards=[
 C('Learn a useful guide and the whole phrase.','Do a task.\nMake a plan.\n\nDo often describes performing an activity; make often describes creating a result. Many choices are established word partnerships, so the meaning guide is not a complete rule.','Learn make a decision, do research and make progress as phrases. A result/activity test cannot explain every collocation on its own.'),
 C('Use do for common work and routine activities.','Do homework / an assignment / research.\nDo the dishes / the laundry / the shopping.\nDo business / your best / someone a favour.\n\nOther verbs may fit too: write a report, take an exam, run errands.','Choose the action the situation actually means. Making an exercise can mean creating it; doing an exercise means completing it.'),
 C('Use make for common outcomes and arrangements.','Make a meal / a coffee / a list.\nMake an appointment / a reservation / a decision.\nMake progress / a mistake / a suggestion.\nMake money / a profit / an offer.','Pay attention to articles: make a decision, but make progress and do homework. Learn the noun’s own countability too.'),
 C('Keep similar business phrases distinct.','We do business with a local supplier. → commercial activity\nWe made a deal yesterday. → a specific agreement\nThey make a living repairing bikes. → earn enough to live\n\nThe nouns guide the established combination.','Do a good job describes performing well. Make something work describes causing a successful result, with a different pattern.'),
 C('Separate auxiliary do from a main verb.','Do you make coffee?\nShe doesn’t do the shopping.\nHe made a mistake, didn’t he?\n\nAuxiliary do forms questions, negatives and tags. Main-verb do names an activity; make may still be the main action.','Do-support does not mean that the main verb must be do. Identify each verb’s job in the sentence.'),
 C('Use do for emphasis or a short reply.','I do appreciate your help. → emphasis\nDoes she make the calls? Yes, she does. → short reply\n\nIn present/past simple, do/does/did can stand in for the main verb or emphasise it.','After did in an emphatic statement, use a base verb: I did make a mistake. Do not use made after the auxiliary did.'),
 C('Recognise causative make.','The notification made me stop.\nWe were made to wait.\n\nActive make + person + base verb expresses a caused or forced action. Its passive uses to + base verb.','This is a grammatical pattern, separate from collocations such as make a phone call. Keep the object and following verb form clear.'),
 C('Judge progress by the work accomplished.','Nathan’s app made planning attractive, but he did not always do the important tasks. Revisit the story with new questions about actions, rewards and actual progress.','When describing your routine, use complete phrases naturally. A longer task list does not by itself show that useful work has been completed.')
];
const tasks=[
 G('choice','Choose the ordinary phrase for reaching a choice.','make a decision','Make a decision is an established collocation for choosing between alternatives.','Learn the verb with the noun.  G('gap','Please ___ your homework before dinner.
